title: Anatomy Image Questions: Landmarks Before Labels
subject: NEET PG Strategy
preview: First locate the region and orientation, then major anatomical landmarks, followed by the target structure.
quickRevision: First locate the region and orientation, then major anatomical landmarks, followed by the target structure.
When possible, infer the image plane and side from relationships rather than memorized colors or labels.
Use the clinical deficit to cross-check anatomical localization.

sections.title: Recognize the question type
points: First locate the region and orientation, then major anatomical landmarks, followed by the target structure.
Identify common adjacent nerves, vessels and surfaces to avoid mistaking a nearby structure.

sections.title: Use this in timed practice
points: When possible, infer the image plane and side from relationships rather than memorized colors or labels.
Use the clinical deficit to cross-check anatomical localization.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not guess from an isolated memorized image without confirming surrounding anatomy.

quiz.question: What should be identified first in an unfamiliar anatomy image?
quiz.explanation: Major landmarks and orientation. First locate the region and orientation, then major anatomical landmarks, followed by the target structure.
